Subject: Post-demo: competitive + incident escalation expectations / next tests

Thanks again for taking the demo today — really useful conversation. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary goals: consistent p95 latency under 300ms for customer-facing chat, control over fallbacks during incidents, and predictable unit cost for high throughput reranking jobs.
- Concern: how Redwood compares vs Bedrock/Vertex on incident handling and RCA cadence (you mentioned the Jan outage at one of the hyperscalers).

Competitive notes (high level)
- Hyperscalers: broad model catalog and integrated infra, but customers report longer RCA windows and opaque rollback criteria for multi-tenant endpoints.
- Redwood: we give per-model SLOs, clear fallback policies (model variant routing), and commit to an RCA within 72 hours for Priority 1 incidents in Dedicated/Private contracts.

Proposed next tests (to prove the differences we discussed)
1) Latency stability test: 8k-token prompt mix, 1–5k qps burst profile; measure cold vs warm p95 and token-cost delta.
2) Incident simulation: simulate a degraded KV cache on a dedicated pool and assert routing/fallback behavior and recovery time.
3) Throughput pricing check: run reranking microbenchmark to estimate tokens/sec cost at different batching settings.

Attachments: comparative matrix + our proposed test plan (see stubs below).

I’ll follow up with scheduling links for the POC runs once Jaspreet confirms the tests.

On Wed, Feb 25, 2026 at 11:07 AM Jaspreet Singh <jaspreet@datasight.ai> wrote:
> For the incident simulation, we need a named escalation contact for P0s. Can you confirm the on-call/escalation flow (who we call after 15 minutes of degradation)?

Hi Jaspreet — quick note on escalation + proposed runbook excerpt (we'll expand in the shared Drive):

Escalation flow (Priority 1)
- 0–15m: automated alert + on-call engineer (SE Ops) triage via PagerDuty.
- 15–60m: if not recovered, escalate to SE Lead + Customer Success lead; parallel mitigation (route to variant / reduce batch size / serve from warm cache).
- 60–72h: RCA draft completed and shared with customer; final RCA sign-off within 72h for Dedicated customers (we can contract to 48h for higher tiers).

Sample RCA contents we’ll produce
- Incident timeline (UTC)
- Triggering event and root cause analysis (including kernel/error traces)
- Mitigation steps taken and config changes applied
- Short/long term fixes + rollout plan
- Artifacts: links to traces, logs, crash dumps, and any diff of model/config used.

Proposed test steps (high level)
1) Provision a small dedicated pool in us-west-2 (we can provision a temporary pool for the test).
2) Run a KV-cache degradation script to simulate intermittent cache evictions for 20 minutes while we send mixed traffic.
3) Measure failover time, proportion of requests routed to fallback model (if any), error rate, and token-cost delta.

I’ve uploaded a draft runbook and the test orchestration script to the shared folder here: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/0B12345/DS-POC-2026 (Sean / test-runbook v1).

If that looks good I can schedule a 90-minute run next Tue or Wed; Vanessa — can you coordinate procurement sign-off?

- Sean
